t: Introduction and overview — Freedom-class Littoral Combat Ship
name: Introduction and overview — Freedom-class Littoral Combat Ship — ship record
title: Introduction and overview — Freedom-class Littoral Combat Ship
description: Introduction and overview of the Freedom-class Littoral Combat Ship: What this class is, its role in the fleet, and why it matters in naval history. The Freedom class — 16 planned — are 3,500-ton littoral combat ships built for speed (47 knots sprint) with swappable mission modules for mine, surface, and anti-submarine warfare. The LCS program faced criticism over survivability and module delays; several early hulls were retired young. Baseline facts: U.S. littoral combat ship; 16 planned; 47-knot sprint; modular missions..
how_it_works: Buoyancy supports the hull; propellers driven by diesel, turbine, or nuclear plant provide thrust; rudders and thrusters steer; stability comes from hull form and ballast.
